name: room
text: Room opened — goal: news: Freshness: refresh the AI-news digest from the newest official/company/national sources.

name: Scoop
text: I’ll pull the freshest AI-news feeds from the last 24 h: run `curl -s https://feeds.bloomberg.com/technology/feed.xml | xq '.rss.channel.item | length'` to count Bloomberg AI items, then `curl -s https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-data-science/news/ | pup 'h2' | wc -l` to tally NVIDIA AI headlines. I’ll save raw XML/HTML to `/tmp/ai-news-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).{xml,html}` and log the counts in `/tmp/ai-news-counts.log`.

name: Factcheck
text: **Factcheck:** Hold on—your Bloomberg feed check is a *length count* on raw XML, not a filtered AI-item tally. That risks conflating AI with general tech noise. And your NVIDIA scrape uses `pup 'h2'`—but NVIDIA’s news page buries AI headlines under "Press Releases" or "Blogs," not just `<h2>` tags. Where’s the validation that these selectors actually capture *AI-specific* content? Show me the filtered output, not just the raw counts.
